During the hearing, learned Counsel for Petitioner made submissions about the issues raised in the Petition. The learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that the present Petition filed by the Petitioners is premature, as CTUIL is yet to take a decision on the inquiry relating to the impugned Show Cause Notices issued to the Petitioners. Considering the submissions of the Petitioners and Respondent, CTUIL, the Commission deemed it appropriate to let CTUIL first conclude its inquiry after following due process in respect of the impugned Show Cause Notices. After inquiry, if CTUIL finds that the connectivity/Petitioner is required to be revoked/blacklisted, CTUIL shall not implement the same for 10 days so that the Petitioner may approach the Commission against the such a decision of CTUIL. _**Issue 1** : Violation of Undertakings qua G1 and G2_ _**Issue 2** : Concealment of material information qua G1_ _**Issue 3** : Eligibility Condition not satisfied for considerable time by G1_ _41. After considering all the material and information presented before it, the factual and legal provisions and in terms of the mandate under the CTU Procedure for Inquiry, CTU’s final recommendation is as below:_ - (i) Accordingly, relying on settled principles governing interim relief and the need to preserve the subject matter of the proceedings, the Applicants pray that this Hon’ble Commission directs CTUIL not to take any coercive or prejudicial action against Ganeko One and Ganeko Two in respect of the Connectivity granted at Mandsaur PS and Solapur PS, pending final adjudication of the Petition. 11. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel of the CTUIL displayed the copy of the revocation letter(s) dated 16.12.2025 vide which the connectivity(ies) of both the Petitioners have been revoked by the CTUIL. CTUIL also informed the Commission that as per direction vide ROP dated 07.08.2025, this revocation would be applicable on 26.12.2025 i.e. after ten (10) days from date of revocation letter i.e. 16.12.2025. Petitioner(s) and the Respondent, CTUIL, concluded their respective arguments during the hearing, considering this Commission reserved the matter for Order and allowed parties to file a brief note of argument. CTUIL was directed to not take any precipitative action against the Petitioner(s) till the final outcome of the Petition. - (a) CTUIL Inquiry Report concluded that there was no fraud. Test of intentionality was not met as the Petitioners had voluntarily disclosed the information on 20.06.2025 Petitioners did not act in ‘transgression to gain an unfair advantage’ as they acted as per the contractual framework without committing any default. 22. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondents and perused the information available on record. The issues which arise for our consideration are as under: **Issue No.1 : Whether the letters dated 29.07.2025 issued to the Petitioners, Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. & Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. by CTUIL are required to be quashed?** ## **Issue No.1 : Whether the letters dated 29.07.2025 issued to the Petitioners, Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. & Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. by CTUIL are required to be quashed?** 27. Petitioner has argued that it got the Base LOA amended to get the location changed by SJVN (REIA) and hence it is not the same LOA. We disagree with such proposition of the Petitioner. In such a situation an entity would get LOA amended a number of times and seek Connectivity for each such LOA and block the Connectivity since under such LOA amended ‘n’ number of times, project shall be installed only at one location. As soon as LOA gets amended, the previous LOA becomes infructuous. entity to go against the Regulations and its undertakings by availing the benefit of an exhausted document. Further assessment of suitability of project for a particular LOA or while seeking Connectivity is solely on Petitioner, and it should have been more prudent when it itself proposed the location to SJVN each time. 41. We would like to clarify that when an entity seeks connectivity, it should make itself aware of the regulations and be serious in implementing the project. The routes have been provided so that all kinds of projects can seek Connectivity. But conversion from land route to LOA route should not be seen as a way out to not furnish the land documents. Without land, in any case entity would not be able to implement the project. We are of the view that since Petitioner was granted Connectivity on Land BG route, it should satisfy the condition of furnishing the land documents. We have already concluded in Issue No1 that Petitioner was in violation of its undertakings while using exhausted documents. Hence, we reject the prayer of Petitioners to permit it to swap the LOAs for purpose of converting its connectivity from LAND BG to LOA route. Hence no direction is required to be issued to CTUIL to consider LOA or PPA for conversion of Connectivity of Petitioner from LAND BG to LOA. The issue of whether Petitioner’s Connectivity should be revoked or not is dealt with in next issue herein. land documents are not in Order, CTUIL shall proceed with the actions in terms of the GNA Regulations. 58.
